blocks.orig: With an area of 988 kilometers squared, this larger island is east of Tanga, or Yambe Island, is recognized for its gentle green hills and clove plantations, and is a great place to see the various fishing and farming villages.
blocks.html: Covering 988 square kilometres, this larger island lies east of Tanga, or Yambe Island. It is known for its soft green hills and clove plantations, and it is a wonderful place to see the many fishing and farming villages.

blocks.orig: Pemba Island is a great destination for those who want more immersion in the people and culture, and you’ll find you have more areas to explore. Each of these is unique as its landscape is brimming with wildlife that you can explore, including Colobus and vervet monkeys, and a wide variety of birds that you’ll hear and see quite easily.
blocks.html: Pemba Island is ideal if you want to immerse yourself more deeply in the people and their culture, and you will find plenty more ground to cover. Every part of it is distinct, with a landscape full of wildlife to discover, from Colobus and vervet monkeys to a huge range of birds that you will hear and spot with ease.

blocks.orig: Additionally, on this island, you’ll find the Kidike Flying Fox Sanctuary, home to 4,000 Pemba flying foxes. You can catch a glimpse of these remarkable bats as you explore the trails within the Ngezi forest. These are just a few of the fascinating sights you’ll encounter here.
blocks.html: On this island you will also come across the Kidike Flying Fox Sanctuary, where 4,000 Pemba flying foxes live. Walk the trails through the Ngezi forest and you may catch sight of these remarkable bats. And that is only a taste of the fascinating things you’ll see here.

blocks.orig: This single small island is located about 3 km off the northeast coast of Zanzibar, which is the largest island in the archipelago. Mnemba Island has a circumference of 1.5 kilometers and can be quiet, with only some staff and a few boats coming and going.
blocks.html: This one small island sits roughly 3 km off the north-east coast of Zanzibar, the largest island in the archipelago. Mnemba Island measures 1.5 kilometres around and tends to be quiet, with just a handful of staff and the occasional boat coming or going.

blocks.orig: This is a private island and only houses 20 guests at a time, but when you’re here, you can find some diverse viewing options so you can enjoy the sea from wherever you are.

blocks.orig: Situated just southeast of Songo Songo Island, accessible via a boat crossing, lies this private island retreat. blocks.orig: Here you can go diving, kayaking, sailing, and snorkeling. You can also discover more about the surrounding area and find out how the local community works. Perhaps you could even get some pointers as you do your own spot of fishing.

blocks.orig: On Fanjove Island, you’ll also find a boutique lodge with bandas that are spread out across the beach and paths that lead to dining areas. Then, you can turn your attention to the nature trails that allow you to explore this rich island more.

blocks.orig: Pungume Island, located south of the village of Fumba, is an area that allows for exploration of the forests and sandbanks. However, during certain times of the year, you can discover a serene and tranquil island, offering fantastic diving opportunities and the chance to witness magnificent whale sharks.
